// A stand-in for `hc` and `herdr-app` (run with node; the .txt name keeps `node --test` from
// treating it as a test file). argv[2] is which tool it plays. All state lives in the JSON
// file named by FAKE_STATE: { labels, tabs: [{ id, name }], calls: [[tool, ...args]] }.
const fs = require("node:fs");

const [, , tool, ...args] = process.argv;
const file = process.env.FAKE_STATE;
const state = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
state.calls.push([tool, ...args]);
const save = () => fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(state));

if (tool === "hc" && args[0] === "get") {
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ address: args[1], labels: state.labels }));
} else if (tool === "hc" && args[0] === "label") {
  const i = args[2].indexOf("=");
  const k = args[2].slice(0, i), v = args[2].slice(i + 1);
  if (v === "") delete state.labels[k]; else state.labels[k] = v;
} else if (tool === "herdr-app" && args[0] === "ls") {
  console.log(JSON.stringify({ spaces: [{ id: "sp1", tabs: state.tabs }] }));
} else if (tool === "herdr-app" && args[0] === "do" && args[1] === "tab.rename") {
  const { id, name } = JSON.parse(args[2]);
  state.tabs.find((t) => t.id === id).name = name;
} else {
  process.exit(1);
}
save();
